Topic: Exploring the 2-adic Metric: A New Way to Measure Distance

Target audience: Undergraduate mathematics students

Section: section_1 — Prerequisite: The Usual Distance

Lecture lines:
Standard distance makes small numbers near zero.
Euclidean metrics show 1/8 as very tiny.
A rabbit hops closer to zero point.

Planned animations:
Create Euclidean number line. Label point 0 in #FFFFFF.
Highlight integers 2, 4, 8, 16 on the line in #FF0000.
Show distance between points shrinking as powers increase.
Draw vector arrows indicating length in #00FF00.
Fade out labels; highlight 0.

Section: section_2 — Introducing the 2-adic Metric

Lecture lines:
2-adic valuation counts prime factors of 2.
High powers of 2 mean smaller norms.
Compare 8 as tiny and 1/8 as large.

Planned animations:
Display prime p=2. Introduce valuation function v_2(x).
Show powers of 2 as "close" to 0.
Highlight the 2-adic metric definition formula in #FFFFFF.
Animate 2^k moving closer to 0 as k increases.
Place "2-adic distance" label in #FFFF00.

Section: section_3 — Infinite Sums and Convergence

Lecture lines:
Convergence means terms approach zero in 2-adic.
Higher powers of 2 stabilize the series.
Adding powers of 2 creates binary towers.

Planned animations:
Visualize partial sums of the geometric series.
Highlight the series 1+2+4+8+... in #FFFFFF.
Animate terms accumulating towards infinity in Euclidean.
Contrast with 2-adic convergence towards a limit.
Highlight the 2-adic limit value -1 in #00FFFF.

Section: section_4 — Visualizing Divergence vs. Convergence

Lecture lines:
Compare standard divergence versus 2-adic convergence.
Ultrametric inequality keeps triangles isosceles here.
1 plus 2 plus 4 equals negative 1.

Planned animations:
Split screen: Euclidean vs. 2-adic metrics.
Animate divergent path in Euclidean side (left).
Animate convergent path in 2-adic side (right).

Section: section_5 — Conclusion and Summary

Lecture lines:
Distance is a flexible, human-defined measurement.
Switching lenses reveals hidden number theory structures.
-1 sits near all powers of 2.

Planned animations:
Flash key terms: Valuation, Metric, Convergence.
Display the final 2-adic number space.
Fade all elements to black.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject
